subthemes.name: Decision making and strategy
subthemes.gist: Papers on reinforcement learning, game theory, and optimization—training agents to make good sequential decisions and play strategic games.

subthemes.name: Knowing when models are uncertain
subthemes.gist: Papers studying how to measure and communicate what a model doesn't know—calibration, uncertainty bounds, and confidence scores that readers can trust.

subthemes.name: Making big models smaller and faster
subthemes.gist: Papers on compressing models and running them efficiently using low-rank updates, mixing specialized experts, or removing unnecessary parameters.

subthemes.name: Sampling and probabilistic inference
subthemes.gist: Papers on generating samples from complex distributions, approximating probability distributions, and efficient Bayesian computation.

subthemes.name: Understanding cause and effect
subthemes.gist: Papers studying causal relationships in data—what causes what, how to infer hidden causes, and how to design experiments and systems that account for causality.

subthemes.name: Continuous learning and adaptation
subthemes.gist: Papers on how models can learn over time without forgetting old knowledge, and how to update models when the world changes without retraining from scratch.

subthemes.name: Matching data across domains
subthemes.gist: Papers on finding similarities between items, matching related data when sources differ, and searching through high-dimensional spaces efficiently.

subthemes.name: Learning from limited labels
subthemes.gist: Papers on training models when you have few labeled examples, by actively choosing which data to label, learning from unlabeled data, or using synthetic data.

subthemes.name: Logical reasoning and theorem proving
subthemes.gist: Papers on making models reason step-by-step through logic puzzles, prove theorems, solve math, and identify errors in their own reasoning.

subthemes.name: Robust and fair predictions
subthemes.gist: Papers on making models work reliably across different groups and conditions, handling noisy data, and making predictions that don't discriminate.
